title: Critical Response Cheat-sheet (personal war-room notes)
content:
Context and goal: quick, portable notes for spinning up a war-room for customer-facing incidents where inference quality or latency is impacting SLAs. Not an official runbook copy — fast checklist + communication templates + follow-ups I can paste into Slack or email.

Top priorities (first 10 mins):
- Confirm scope: which customer, which route/model, affected endpoints, severity (S1/S2).
- Post to #cs-escalations: short headline + initial tags. Use template below.
- Assign roles (owner, SRE lead, eng on-call, CS lead). Capture in thread.
- Stabilize: throttle/redirect traffic if hit surge; apply immediate rate-limiting or fallback to model-variant if available.
- Capture logs + start timeline (t=0). Ensure request IDs captured.

Quick triage checklist (ordered):
1) Reproduce with cURL (token masked) or dev sandbox: quantify error rate / latency distribution.
2) Check model health dashboard (console > per-route latency, error breakdown).
3) Look at GPU capacity in Dedicated pools & recent autoscale events.
4) Inspect KV/prefix-cache hit rate and recent cache evictions.
5) Confirm any config changes or rollouts in last 24h (Console rollout history, PRs).

Immediate mitigation options (pick fastest):
- Switch route to stable model-variant (low-risk). NOTE: check quantization/profile compat.
- Reduce max_tokens / response length hints for affected route.
- Enable temporary rate-limit for non-critical customers.
- Deploy quick hotfix (small prompt rewrite) to reduce degenerate generation loops.

Communications templates (pasteable):
- Slack (initial): "[INCIDENT] Customer <ACME INC> seeing high latency on /v1/generate (model: rdl-13b-quant). Investigating. Own: @Sofia. SRE: @Evan. Please avoid pushing changes to model rollouts until clear."
- Email to customer (short): "Hi <Name> — we see increased latency impacting your requests. We are actively investigating and have a dedicated team working on mitigation. I'll send a status update in 20 minutes and share a timeline. — Sofia (CS Lead)"

Data to capture (must-have):
- Example request IDs (3), timestamps, input size, model variant, route config, observed latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), error messages.
- Recent deploys/rollout IDs (Console > Rollouts).

Roles // who to ping first (personal list):
- Owner/Incident lead: Sofia Patel (me)
- SRE lead: Evan Martinez
- Serving runtime eng: Rina Gupta
- Model ops: Carlos Mendes
- Customer success contact: account team (linked in CRM)

Rapid debugging commands (notes I can run locally or paste):
- curl -H "Authorization: Bearer X" -d @sample.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --include
- kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving -l app=model-runtime --sort-by=.status.startTime
- gcloud compute instances list --filter="name~'rdw-dedicated'" (if on GCP)

Decision matrix (if mitigation not immediate):
- If p99 latency > 5s for >10% of requests and customer paying SLA => escalate to exec-on-call and enable dedicated fallback route.
- If quality regression observed (bad hallucinations) and rollback possible => initiate rollback and lock new prompts.

Notes to self (questions to ask in war-room):
- Any ongoing A/B or canary on that model? (PRs: check GH and Console rollouts)
- Recent infra maintenance windows? (SRE calendar)
- Is this reproducible across regions or only single region?

Immediate action items (fill during meeting):
- [ ] Collect 3 example request IDs (owner: ???, due: +10m)
- [ ] Post initial incident message to #cs-escalations (owner: Sofia, done: no)
- [ ] Check Console for model rollouts (owner: Rina, due: +5m)
- [ ] Lock model rollout if suspect (owner: Rina/Evan, due: +15m)
- [ ] Enable fallback-route if latency persists (owner: Evan, due: +20m)

Follow-up / Post-meeting items (populate after resolution):
- Create incident ticket RED-XXXX in JIRA with timeline and root cause hypothesis.
- Plan remediation: config change, model retrain or rollback, runtime patch. Owners + ETA.
- Post-mortem draft due in 72 hours. Assign author.
- Update console rollout safeguards (add extra gating) if rollout caused incident.

Escalation contacts (fast dial):
- Pager: Evan Martinez (SRE) — oncall@sre.redwood.ai (add phone)
- Eng leads: Rina, Carlos (Slack handles in doc above)

Risk and recovery notes:
- Risk: fallback variant may have slightly different tokenization/behavior — call out to CS if output format changes.
- Recovery: verify cache priming after switching variant to avoid cold-KV penalty.

Post-resolution check (quick):
- Verify p50/p95/p99 back to baseline for 30m.
- Customer confirmation: send note with timeline + actions + next steps.
- Convert personal notes into runbook changes (if any) and link PR.

Misc scratch ideas for longer term:
- Add automated route-level circuit-breaker in gateway when p99 > threshold.
- Better telemetry around prefix cache eviction events and per-tenant cache stats.
- Canary gating that checks both latency and token-level quality metrics before a rollout reaches 100%.

Open questions (to resolve in follow-up):
- Was there a correlated spike in prefix-cache evictions? (need metrics)
- Did any quantized kernel change land in last deploy window? (check GH commit log)
- Should we add a temporary customer-specific SLA credit in severe cases? (CS policy)

My immediate next steps if I start this war-room alone:
1) Post initial Slack message with owners.
2) Grab sample IDs and ask Rina to check rollout history.
3) Ask Evan to check Dedicated capacity and consider fallback routing.
4) Keep customer updated every 20 minutes until stable.

-- end of cheat-sheet.

Notes: this is my scratch copy. After the incident I'll prune into a tidy runbook entry and link to RED-XXXX.
